Lauren / team — joined the bridge. Quick findings from initial triage:
- Pool utilization: reserved pool for Clearbridge saturated at ~99% for last 25 mins. Spillover is queueing at the front of the routing tier.
- Noisy-tenant: one other tenant on the same pool is spiking short-lived bursts (identified tenant-id t-8712). We can throttle that tenant in ~6 mins with a config flip.
- KV cache behavior: we see an increase in KV cache misses correlated with long-context tokenization; this increases per-request compute by ~15-25%.

Immediate remediation (can execute in the next 10-15 mins):
1) Apply noisy-tenant soft-throttle (prevent it from acquiring new slots) — low risk, immediate.
2) Enable fallback routing to quantized model variant (redwood-llama-v2-13b-q4f) for non-critical long-context requests — reduces latency but may change output quality (~2-3% regression on eval prompts).
3) Provision +30% burst capacity to Clearbridge's reservation for the next 6 hours while we root cause (requires exec approval to apply billable burst in account).

Cost implication estimate for burst: ~$2.4k/hour at current usage (approx $14.4k for 6 hours). If we proceed, we should request exec sign-off and confirm whether to bill or apply one-off credit.

I will proceed with (1) and (2) now unless anyone objects. For (3) I need explicit authorization from a manager/exec.

Command snippets:
- throttle: infractl tenant throttle --tenant t-8712 --limit soft
- fallback routing toggle: infractl routing set-fallback --account clearbridge --model redwood-llama-v2-13b-q4f

— David
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
